findings.title: Queries are interpolated twice in shard splitting path
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery now interpolates targets with applyTemplateVariables. The sharded sub-requests are then passed to runSplitQuery, which this PR also changed to call applyTemplateVariables on every target. Each query is therefore interpolated twice: once in the shard path and once in the time-splitting path. The second pass can re-expand already-substituted text or variable-like content (for example filters or ad-hoc filters applied twice), and it costs extra work per sub-request. The updated test even expects applyTemplateVariables to be called 5 times.

findings.title: applyTemplateVariables runs before the hidden/empty filtering is relied upon and may mutate inputs
findings.body: The interpolated result replaces the original queries, so later grouping, tracking and the sub-request targets use interpolated expressions. Any downstream code that relies on the raw expression, such as trackGroupedQueries or the backend's interval variable handling for $__auto and $__interval, now sees substituted values. Per the added test, $__auto becomes a fixed value on the frontend. The test mocks also mutate the query in place, which hides whether the real implementation copies it.

findings.title: Test asserts an implementation-detail call count
findings.body: The assertion toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5) bakes in the double interpolation (one call in the shard path plus one per sub-request through runSplitQuery). It is brittle and legitimizes the redundant work instead of asserting that interpolation happens before execution.
